description: We are building AstroVitals, a health-monitoring platform for astronauts on long missions. It will track sleep, fatigue, stress, activity, nutrition, and well-being using daily check-ins, dashboards, and alerts, with actionable recommendations. I am a CSE student interested in full-stack development, data visualization, and AI. We welcome teammates in web, UI/UX, data/ML, research, storytelling, or video.
summary: ASTRAGUARD is an astronaut health-monitoring support system designed to help astronauts and crew medical officers review health information during long-duration space missions. The platform brings together physiological readings, daily wellness check-ins, health history, trend visualisations and configurable demonstration alerts in one dashboard. Its interactive 2D human-body map allows users to explore different body systems and view related monitoring information. ASTRAGUARD uses synthetic demonstration data to show how health records can be organised, reviewed and tracked over time. Inspired by NASA's human-spaceflight research, the project aims to make health information easier to understand and support informed monitoring and communication between crew members and medical teams.
details:
ASTRAGUARD is a web-based astronaut health-monitoring support platform developed to demonstrate how crew health information can be organised and reviewed during long-duration space missions.

The application provides separate views for astronauts and crew medical officers. Users can record physiological readings such as heart rate, blood pressure, oxygen saturation and body temperature, complete daily wellness check-ins, and review historical records. A dashboard presents key readings and trends, while an interactive 2D human-body map lets users explore cardiovascular, respiratory, neurological and thermal monitoring categories. A configurable demonstration rule system highlights readings that fall outside the project's example ranges, and alerts can be reviewed and acknowledged.

The project is designed to make health information easier to access, understand and communicate. Its creative element is the combination of a visual 2D body map, individual health records, trend views and crew-oriented monitoring in one interface.

The application is developed using React, Vite, Tailwind CSS, JavaScript, Node.js, Express.js and MongoDB. The team considered usability, clear visual feedback, role-based access and the limitations of remote health monitoring. The current demonstration uses synthetic data and is not a medical diagnostic or treatment system.
